Mobilising International Opinion on Hijacking of IA Plane 
*1. SHRI E. BALANANDAN: Will the Minister of EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) what political pressure, in view of the hijacking of Indian Airlines, 
flight, had been mounted in mobilising international opinion on hijackers' 
mentors' in Pakistan and the Taliban authorities; 
(b) whether Government are aware that the United St ates took full four 
days to react to the hijacking and UK have been conspicuous by not stating 
anything and there was lukewarm response from other Western powers that 
provided sustenance to the hijackers; and 
(c) if so, the reaction of the Government thereto? 
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI JASWANT 
SINGH): (a) An exercise to inform international public opinion was put into 
operation immediately after the hijacking of IC-814 occurred. 
External Affairs Minister personally contacted several of his 
counterparts in the international community. This included the neighbouring 
countries, member countries in the UN Security Council and the Foreign 
Ministers of Governments with nationals aboard the hijacke aircraft. Foreign 
Secretary was also in touch with some of 
his counterparts abroad and with the Heads of Diplomatic Missions in Delhi. 
In all instances, pledges of support and cooperation were received. All 
governments expressed their support for any decision that would eventually 
be taken to ensure the safety of passengers and to terminate the hijacking. All 
our foreign interlocutors expressed their understanding of the difficult choices 
the Government of India faced in dealing with the incident. After the arrival 
of the hijacked aircraft at Kandahar, at India's r equest, countries whose 
nationals were aboard the aircraft sent special emissaries also to Kandahar. 
(b) International support for India, and condemnation of the hijacking, 
was further elaborated in official statements issued by several foreign 
Governments. These official statements left no doubt that  the  hijacking  of 
IC-814  represented  an  unacceptable  act of 
8 

[24 February, 2000] RAJYA SABHA 
international terrorism, also that any action undertaken by the Indian 
Government would receive their full support. 
(c) Government have brought to the attention of the international 
community the role played by Pakistan in the hijacking. Government have 
raised the matter with the Government of Pakistan and have provided 
evidence to them of the involvement of the ir nationals in the hijacking. The 
hijackers are believed to be currently in Pakistan. Government have 
reminded the Government of Pakistan that as a signatory to several 
International Conventions against Terrorism, also the Simla Agreement of 
1972, and the  Lahore Declaration, it has an international obligation to take 
the hijackers into custody and to extradite them to India. The Government of 
Pakistan, in its response, has reiterated its general position that it would 
undertake to apprehend and prosecute any person or persons found on its 
territory or the territory of Pakistan -Occupied Kashmir who may be 
suspected of having committed such offences related to hijacking. As they 
have at the same time rejected our demarche, Pakistan's general commitment 
is of little value. 
Government have also raised the matter with the International Civil 
Aviation Organisation (ICAO) with the view to bring to the attention of the 
member countries the need to adopt appropriate measures to apprehend and 
extradite the hijackers to India. 
The Taliban authorities, while adopting an attitude of correct 
facilitators, consistently had their sympathies with the hijackers and their 
other supporters. 
The hijacking incident also highlighted to the international community 
evidence of Pakist an's continued state sponsorship of terrorism, and its 
attempts to interfere in the internal affairs of India. The international 
community now better recognises Pakistan's state sponsorship of terrorism 
and the impact this has on the security of India and the region. This 
increased awareness is now reflected in both official statements by 
spokesmen of foreign Governments and the coverage of the international 
media.

Propagation of Internet Education 
*3. SHRI RAMACHANDRA KHU NTIA: Will the Minister of 
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) what steps Government have taken or propose to take to propagate 
internet education, considering the vast potentiality of information 
technology; 
(b) whether Government have any plans to se t any Authority/ company 
exclusively for the purpose and launch centrally sponsored schemes for 
states; and 
(c) what steps Government have taken or propose to take to provide 
computer/computer education in States? 
THE MINISTER OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS AND 
MINISTER OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (SHRI PRAMOD 
MAHAJAN): (a) Government have been taking initiatives from time to time 
for promoting Internet based education. This includes online learning by 
supporting a Virtual Campus Initiative at Indira Gandhi National Op en 
University for a One Year Post -Graduate Diploma Course in Information 
Technology. The Government is also funding the development of Web-
based/Multi-media courseware at two HTs at Delhi and Kanpur and the Birla 
Institute of Technology and Science, Pilani. 
(b) No, Sir. 
(c) Existing Engineering Colleges and Universities offer a range of 
formal courses in the area of computer sciences, electronics and information 
technology. Department of Electronics Accreditation Computer Courses 
(DOEACC), a society set up under th e aegis of Ministry of Information 
Technology and the All India Council of Technical Education (AICTE) 
conducts four levels of courses for the non -formal sector at a national level. 
Similarly, two societies of Ministry of Information Technology, namely, 
Centre for Electronics Design & Technology of India (CEDTI) and Centre 
for Development of Advanced Computing (C -DAC) have launched 
nationwide franchising schemes to promote IT Education in this country.
